methodological_rigor.justification: Large retrospective cohort study (n=12,360 MM patients, 320 receiving CAR-T) from UC Health system (2021-2025). Primary analysis: logistic regression with adjustment for age, gender, ADI, insurance, UC location, CRAB features, ISS stage, race, ethnicity. Appropriate statistical methods: generalized linear model (GLM), odds ratios with 95% CIs, significance defined as CI not spanning 1 and p<0.05. Secondary analysis: zero-shot GPT-4 inference on clinical notes (n=270 patients, 417 notes) to assess CAR-T discussions and eligibility. However, selection bias from inclusion criteria (patients with insurance, complete ADI score, visit ≥Jan 2021); ISS staging incomplete (7.5% missing); temporal heterogeneity (2021-2025 period with evolving CAR-T indications); GPT-4 validation limited to subsample.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study (LoE 2b) examining treatment disparities in CAR-T therapy access among MM patients. High clinical relevance: addresses health equity concerns in innovative cancer therapy delivery; identifies patients who may be eligible but not offered advanced treatment. Patterns detected (race, treatment location) have direct implications for health system redesign and care pathways. However, study is observational and documents associations rather than establishing causal mechanisms; limited insight into modifiable barriers.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-compliant reporting with clear study design, participant selection from UC Health Data Warehouse, inclusion/exclusion criteria detailed. Methods comprehensively described including variable definitions (ISS staging, CRAB features, insurance types, ADI calculation). Statistical approach explicitly stated (GLM, p-value significance thresholds). However, no data availability statement regarding UCHDW access or code availability. GPT-4 prompting strategy detailed but model validation approach limited (subsample comparison to ground truth not fully specified).

novelty_literature.justification: Novel application: first study combining large EHR cohort analysis with LLM-based clinical note analysis to detect CAR-T access disparities and undiscussed eligibility. Prior work documented racial disparities in MM outcomes and access to ASCT; this study extends to CAR-T era with innovative NLP methodology. Demonstrates geographic variation in CAR-T administration and identifies specific barriers (referral, documentation, communication) contributing to disparities. Integration of GPT-4 for eligibility determination and discussion identification represents methodological advance in health equity research.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript clearly establishing motivation (higher MM burden in Black patients; limited CAR-T access). Methods logically presented with data warehouse description, population selection, and statistical approach. Results systematically organized with baseline characteristics, univariate/multivariate associations, and location-specific patterns. Incorporation of GPT-4 results appropriately contextualized with acknowledgment of limitations. Discussion thoughtfully interprets disparities, distinguishing biological from structural/system-level factors; acknowledges alternative hypotheses (undocumented discussions, patient preferences) and study limitations (temporal heterogeneity, neighborhood-level SES proxy limitations).

key_strengths: Large population-based cohort (n=12,360) from integrated UC Health system spanning three academic centers with CAR-T capacity; addresses important equity question in real-world setting

Clear identification of disparities: Black patients 67% less likely to receive CAR-T (OR 0.33); location-dependent variation (UC-3 58% less likely than UC-1); disparities persist after adjustment for disease severity and insurance

Novel methodological approach: GPT-4 zero-shot learning applied to clinical notes identifies eligible patients lacking documented CAR-T discussions (50% of Other Pacific Islander, 4.2% Black, 0.6% White); highlights potential referral/documentation gaps
Comprehensive covariate adjustment including disease severity (ISS stage, CRAB features), socioeconomic status (ADI), insurance coverage, and demographic factors
key_concerns: Retrospective observational study unable to establish causation; cannot determine whether disparities reflect clinical decision-making, patient preferences, undocumented discussions, or structural barriers
Selection bias from inclusion criteria (patients with insurance, complete ADI, documented treatments); excludes uninsured and may underrepresent socioeconomically disadvantaged populations
Incomplete ISS staging (7.5% missing) due to absent beta-2 microglobulin measurements; revised ISS not applicable; limits prognostic stratification granularity

GPT-4 eligibility assessment limited to UCSF (270 patients); validation approach not fully detailed; potential for model hallucination in interpreting clinical notes not addressed; small sample sizes by race category limit precision
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 3 observational health equity study appropriate for general oncology or specialty hematology journal. Leverages EHR infrastructure and innovative NLP methodology to identify care gaps. Retrospective design and causal inference limitations prevent higher tier. Results support need for system-level intervention and improved care navigation for CAR-T therapy access.
